accuracy.why: Every clause of each English string and its Arabic is in the Urdu, and nothing is added (stage 4 fence, 15 phrases; stage 3 added no fact): the attractions on the map of the oasis, named as N47 rules («الاحساء کے نخلستان»); search or choose a category; a place chosen in the list or on the map opens its card; the empty notice with its category branch; the counter names what it counts as the Arabic does («المعالم الظاهرة», not the English verb); the locate button and the list region as the source names them; the popup link with «←». Two points off: “card” is said by what it holds («مختصر تعارف», N306: no «کارڈ»), and the Arabic’s two verbs (choose a category / press a place) are one Urdu verb after round 1 — no native device-neutral verb for “press a link” exists in the line’s evidence (N89, P16-test), so the distinction is carried by the objects, not the verbs.

nativeness.why: The reader passed the lead’s facts, the empty notice, the counter and the save and location messages as natural (item 21) and raised nothing on the title, the eyebrow, the search field, the chip «سب», the list label or the popup link. Round 1 answers his two moderate charges in scope with the smallest edits («چنیں» for «منتخب کریں», «تین جہتی» for «سہ جہتی»), both unverified until the fresh read. Four points off for what still stands: «زمین کے نشیب و فراز» is the bookish half of item 5 and no plainer attested native phrase for terrain is in evidence (two points); the label of the chip group keeps the noun «انتخاب» beside the verb «چنیں» (item 19, minor, one point); the locate label is a bare noun phrase that does not say what the button does (item 8, minor; the source’s form, one point).

compliance.why: Letterforms, digits and punctuation clean (stage 5: codepoints none, 407 scanned; ھ only after aspirable letters); «الاحساء» byte for byte in the ruled possessive (P2, P8, N47); approved text reused byte for byte (map.eyebrow = list.eyebrow «سیاحتی معلومات», N190/N191; map.search.ph = list.search; map.empty = search.empty + the category branch; «سیاحتی مقامات» as nav.attractions; the arrow as det.allSights); P16 held (no «کارڈ», «ٹیپ», «کلک», «تھری ڈی», «شیئر»); N308 held (no language note on the link to the English terrain page); {n} once. One point off: «تین جہتی» has no dictionary headword of its own (Rekhta has «سہ جہتی»; the compound of «تین» and «جہتی» is attested in use only), and the masculine of «انتخاب» was inferred at stage 5, not read on an entry.

fit.why: The traveller learns how many places the map holds, how to narrow them and how to open one; the counter is spoken after every filter; the empty notice tells him what to change. One point off: the terrain link opens an English page with an Urdu label (N308, owner_decision: no language note), and the locate button’s label leaves its action to the button role (item 8).

calibration.question: map.terrain: how is “3D” said in Urdu, where no Latin letter is allowed (EN “3D terrain map”, AR «الخريطة التضاريسية 3D»)?
candidates: A «سہ جہتی» — «زمین کے نشیب و فراز کا سہ جہتی نقشہ» (stages 1–5).
B «تھری ڈی» — the English letters spelled in Urdu script.
C «تین جہتی» — «زمین کے نشیب و فراز کا تین جہتی نقشہ».
calibration.evidence: Stage 4 (s45-web.json, HTTP 200): A Rekhta headword «سَہ جِہَتی» “three dimensional”, ur.wikipedia 41 pages, «سہ جہتی نقشہ» 1 (چندریان-2); B 607 pages, film formats and product names, no headword, «تھری ڈی نقشہ» 0; C 37 pages, among them the reference article «نقشہ» («… دو جہتی ہوتے ہیں، تین جہتی …»); D 18, mathematics and physics. Re-counted by the judge 2026-10-16 (s7-web.json, HTTP 200): «تین جہتی» 37 (top titles کرہ ارض · نقشہ · تصویر), «سہ جہتی» 41, «تین جہتی نقشہ» 0; Rekhta has no entry page for «تین جہتی» (two slugs tried redirect to the home page), its entry «سہ جہتی» answers (Adjective, “three dimensional”). Blind reader on-05, item 5 (moderate): «سہ جہتی» and «نشیب و فراز» “bookish and over-Persianized”, read twice to see a 3D terrain map; his «3D نقشہ» is Latin.
calibration.stage4_recommendation: A stays; C is the fallback if the blind reader finds «سہ» bookish or unknown.
calibration.ruling_or_recommendation: C: «تین جہتی» — map.terrain «زمین کے نشیب و فراز کا تین جہتی نقشہ». The reader’s charge is the condition stage 4 set for the fallback, and between two native words a reader’s stumble is evidence (the restriction of P16 is on loans). C is the plainer of the two, the wording the reference article on maps uses, and needs no Latin letter and no figure. B refused: P16-test (2) is now met, but (1) is not (the reference names 3D maps natively, A and C) and (3) is not (no headword); a stumble alone never admits a loan. A withdrawn from this string; it stays a correct headword and is recorded in C’s entry for search. D not taken (technical). Cost, charged: «تین جہتی» has no headword of its own (both parts are common words; the compound is attested in use), and «تین» could be read as a count beside «نشیب و فراز» (not reported). Unverified until the proof pass and the fresh blind read on r1.

تین جہتی.source: ur.wikipedia exact phrase «تین جہتی» 37 pages, top titles کرہ ارض · نقشہ · تصویر (HTTP 200, 2026-10-16, stage 4 s45-web.json and judge s7-web.json); the reference article «نقشہ» uses it of maps («بہت سے نقشے جامد دو جہتی ہوتے ہیں، تین جہتی …», stage 4). تین جہتی.note: STAGE 7 (b21-ui, round 1): N331 C ruled, replacing the stage-1/4 proposal «سہ جہتی» in map.terrain after the on-05 blind reader called it bookish (item 5). Verified on HTTP-200 usage attestation (ur.wikipedia, the reference article on maps); no entry page of its own: nothing more is claimed. An invariable adjective: the gender field is formal, «مذکر» being the gender of the noun it qualifies in its one use, «نقشہ».
